text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE

- The OSCE ambassador in Tirana Herbert Grubmayer said the OSBE observers will stop monitoring the polling stations after 6 p.m.. According to the current electoral law, voting will end only at 9 p.m.

- The Socialist Party, Social Democratic Party, Human Rights Party and Democratic Alliance Party will form the government resulting from June 29 elections, Democratic alliance Party leader Neritan Ceka said in an interview.
- Full-page report on intelligence secret service (Shik) activity in Vlore before the rebellion, showing Shik was allegedly trying to find links between demonstrators and foreign circles.
- Shijak TV, the first Albanian private television station, is about to shut down due to lack of investment.
- Five policemen were injured in Tirana after a gunfight.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- Leaders of the main Democratic and Socialist parties signed a pact vowing they will not contest elections outcome.
- "I pledge to re-establish order and calm in three months," Albania's king Leka Zogu, seeking support for restoration of monarchy, said in the central town of Elbasan.
- President Sali Berisha finally agreed to meet calls by the International Monetary Fund and World Bank to enact a law on transparency over pyramid investment schemes.
- An Italian businessman in the northern town of Lac killed three people who were trying to loot his warehouse.
- Doctors fear a possible cholera outbreak.
ALBANIA

- President Sali Berisha turned down an invitation to attend the Crans Montana forum in Switzerland set for June 28, saying he wanted to remain in Albania for the elections and share the joy of victory with supporters of his Democratic Party.

- Final dissolution of so-called committees of public salvation and re-establishment of legal state and local authorities are essential for free and fair elections, according to a statement of the European Democratic Union, grouping Europe's Christian Democrats.
- Police are going to guard polling stations, not the Alba multinational force, paper says.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- The Socialist Party will not benefit from the votes of red gangs, President Sali Berisha told his Democratic Party's supporters during an electoral rally in Tirana.
- Socialist Party armed gangs terrorised Tropoje residents ahead of a rally led by Berisha in the town main square.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- Voting for Socialist Party means voting for Albania's future and integration with European institutions, the party leader Fatos Nano told a crowd northern town of Kruje.
